# QS-CFW-4068-79 - Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-4068-79 (52100)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3  
Part: CFW-4068-79

Scope
This quality specification defines mandatory acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-4068-79 forged from steel grade 52100. It applies to all forgings produced at Plant P3 for this part number and to any subcontracted forging operations performed on behalf of Cascade Forge Works. The intent is to ensure consistent hardness, dimensional control, and safe forging mass prior to subsequent machining and heat treatment operations.

Background and rationale
Bearing rings for this product are critical components in rotating assemblies. Control of hardness and bore geometric stability entering the machine shop reduces scrap and rework, improves bearing life, and lowers total cost. The specified hardness range balances wear resistance and toughness for the selected steel grade. The specified bore tolerance ensures proper running clearance after finishing operations. The maximum forging weight is defined to ensure safe handling and to match the capabilities of in-plant forging and handling equipment.

Requirements table
The table below lists the mandatory acceptance criteria to be verified for each production lot. Any item not clearly conforming to the stated requirement must be recorded and handled per the nonconformance handling section.

| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material grade | 52100 |
| Part identification | CFW-4068-79 |
| Hardness (as-formed or after specified heat operation prior to final machining) | 35-40 HRC |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.07 mm |
| Maximum forging weight | 91.7 kg |
| Surface condition | Free of seams, laps, and forging defects that jeopardize machinability or integrity; machining allowance maintained where applicable |
| Identification marking | Legible part and heat traceability marking per plant marking standard |

Inspection method
General principles
Inspections shall be carried out by trained quality personnel or designated inspectors. Inspectors shall use calibrated equipment traceable to applicable calibration standards maintained by Plant P3. When sampling is used, samples shall be representative of the production lot and the sampling rationale shall be documented in the inspection record.

Hardness verification
Hardness shall be measured on the forged ring at locations that are representative of the bore region and the ring cross section. Measurements shall be made using an instrument appropriate for HRC scale. The measured hardness values must fall within the specified hardness range of 35-40 HRC. If initial measurements are outside of this range, additional discrete measurements shall be made across the ring to assess the extent of deviation. Records shall state measured locations, measured values, instrument identification, and operator identification.

Bore tolerance verification
Bore diameter shall be measured using an appropriate internal sizing method capable of resolving the required tolerance. Measurement shall confirm the bore is within the specified tolerance of ±0.07 mm relative to the nominal drawing dimension. For rings with interrupted or out-of-round conditions, multiple measurements in different radial positions shall be recorded. The measurement technique and instrument used shall be recorded on the inspection record.

Mass verification
The forging weight shall be checked to ensure the forging does not exceed the maximum forging weight of 91.7 kg. Scales used for mass verification must be calibrated and traceable to plant calibration records. Where a forging is found above the maximum forging weight, it shall be segregated and processed through the nonconformance workflow.

Surface and visual inspection
All forgings shall be visually inspected for surface discontinuities, laps, cracks, and foreign material that may affect subsequent processing. Inspectors shall verify machining allowance areas are intact and that no scarfing removed required stock. Visual inspection findings shall be annotated in the inspection record and supported with photographic evidence for any indication graded as potentially consequential.

Sampling and documentation
When full inspection of each item is impractical, a documented sampling justification must be attached to the lot inspection record. The sampling justification shall include the lot definition and the rationale for the selected sample items. For each inspected item, the inspection record shall include identification of the part, material heat number, measured values for each characteristic, instrument identifiers, inspector initials, and disposition.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
Any forging that fails to meet any requirement in the requirements table shall be marked and segregated immediately from conforming material. Segregation shall prevent inadvertent use of nonconforming forgings in production.

Disposition options
Disposition of nonconforming forgings shall follow one of the documented options: rework, scrap, or use as-is under authorized concession. Rework proposals must include a documented method and verification steps demonstrating the final part will meet all specified requirements. Scrap must be processed per plant material control procedures. Use-as-is concessions require formal engineering authorization and must reference the specific deviation and the risk mitigation plan.

Documentation and records
All nonconformances shall be recorded in the plant quality system with a description of the nonconformance, measured evidence, photographs where applicable, proposed disposition, and final approval. Records shall include the inspector name, date of discovery, associated heat number, and disposition authority. For any concession granted, the record shall include the justification, engineering approval, and any applicable customer notification.

Examples
Example 1: A forging shows local hardness readings below the specified range. The inspector documents measurement points and values, segregates the lot, and initiates an investigation. If heat treatment correction is feasible and documented to restore hardness into 35-40 HRC, rework may be permitted with verification testing.

Example 2: A forging measures outside the bore tolerance of ±0.07 mm in one radial position. The inspector records multiple radial measurements, marks the part as nonconforming, and proposes corrective machining. Corrective machining shall be evaluated to ensure final geometry will meet drawing requirements and is documented prior to release.

Records to keep
- Lot inspection report including part identification CFW-4068-79 and material 52100.  
- Hardness measurement log with instrument identifiers and measured values.  
- Bore measurement records with instrument identification and measured locations.  
- Mass verification record showing measured mass versus maximum forging weight 91.7 kg.  
- Nonconformance reports and disposition records, including photographic evidence and engineering approvals.

Approval and implementation
This specification is effective at Plant P3 for all production and subcontract forgings of CFW-4068-79. Compliance with the listed requirements is mandatory; deviations require formal engineering concession and documented approval.
